cards.subject: Kel'Theril
lines: A Highborne city. Its people stole the Crystal of Zin-Malor from Azshara, played with it, and shattered it — and the shattering cursed them.
The Sundering dropped what was left under water and the water froze. When you walk out onto that ice you are standing on a roof.

cards.subject: It happened twice
lines: About a century before the game, high elves came down from Quel'Thalas looking for the crystal's shards.
They are ghosts in the same ruins now.
Two sets of dead elves, ten thousand years apart, same mistake, same ice.

cards.subject: The furbolgs are drugged
lines: A satyr brewed it out of corrupted Felwood matter and gave it to the Winterfall for exactly this reason. It is addictive and it makes them paranoid.
Players farmed the bottles as a cheap attack power buff.
What you get out of one is half what they get.

cards.subject: Timbermaw Post
lines: The camp on the road west of the lake is named for the friendly furbolgs, and it is held by the corrupted Winterfall, who took it.
The name is the only thing left of who lived there.
The corruption in this zone is not finished. It is still moving.

cards.subject: Two exalted grinds for one cat
lines: Rivern Frostwind sits on top of Frostsaber Rock and will not sell you one until you are Exalted. Then he charges a hundred gold.
Anyone who is not a night elf needs Exalted with Darnassus for the riding skill on top of that.
It is hundreds of runs, and it is the most notorious grind in the game.

cards.subject: The grind runs on the drug
lines: The quests that buy the cat are meat runs and Winterfall killing — and the firewater comes off the same furbolgs.
You clear out a tribe somebody else poisoned in order to be sold a cat.

cards.subject: Everlook has nobody in charge
cards.tag: The only goblin town without a boss
lines: Ratchet, Gadgetzan and Booty Bay each have a named goblin running them. Everlook does not, and the wiki can only guess at who it might be.
The goblins are up here for the last untapped thorium and arcanite on the continent.
Neutrality is the price of the ore.

cards.subject: Steam in a zone that never thaws
lines: Donova Snowden camps beside boiling pools in the far west of a permanently frozen zone and cannot explain them.
Her working theory is demonic bleed-through from Darkwhisper Gorge, right across the map.
Water from these pools is what purifies the firewater.

cards.subject: A satyr who will talk to you
lines: Neutral to both factions, standing at the night elf temple ruins, handing out blacksmithing quests — in a game where satyrs are otherwise always hostile.
He speaks Eredun at you unprompted: "Aman asj ze sorankar, karkun."
He is named after the Dr. Seuss character.

cards.subject: Onyxia's key ends in a cave up here
lines: You cannot walk to Haleh. You step onto a portal rune on the floor at the deepest point of the cave and it takes you to her.
She is Malygos's consort, and the first consort ever to outlive an Aspect.
The Alliance side of the Drakefire Amulet finishes with her.

cards.subject: Darkwhisper Gorge
lines: Demons that survived Archimonde's defeat at Hyjal retreated down the ravine in the far east and are still in it.
The Twilight's Hammer only take the gorge in Cataclysm. In here it is the Burning Legion.
Elite, five-man difficulty, outdoors, with no instance portal anywhere.

cards.subject: Thunderfury's smelter lives among them
lines: The high elf who teaches the skill stands inside Darkwhisper Gorge, in the middle of the demons.
Every Thunderfury in vanilla came through this spot.
So did the warlocks and priests farming the gorge for their epic chains.

cards.subject: The yetis were incidental
lines: The cave south-east of Everlook had thorium inside it and one of vanilla's Black Lotus spawn points at its mouth.
That herb gated every raid flask on the server.
People did not camp this cave for the yetis.
